pr_title: [Merged by Bors] - allow up to 16 parameters for systems
pr_body:
fixes #1772 

1st commit: the limit was at 11 as the macro was not using a range including the upper end. I changed that as it feels the purpose of the macro is clearer that way.

2nd commit: as suggested in the `// TODO`, I added a `Config` trait to go to 16 elements tuples. This means that if someone has a custom system parameter with a config that is not a tuple or an `Option`, they will have to implement `Config` for it instead of the standard `Default`.
pr_comments:
I don't think the `Config` trait is the correct solution here.

Iirc, in my implementation of this, I used a method to create the default config on `SystemParam` (which would be on `SystemParamState` in this case). This has the advantage of not placing any requirements (beyond `Send`+`Sync`) on the `Config` type. This avoids `Local` being 'magical', in that it can get `Config` implemented for `Option`, but a third party type couldn't do the equivalent for say `Result` because of the orphan rule.

> I don't think the `Config` trait is the correct solution here.

Completely agree with your issue and idea 👍

Pull request successfully merged into main.

issue_context.title: Weird limits on tuple parameters
issue_context.body:
After the new ECSv2 overhaul, the limit for the number of system and query parameters was reduced from the old limit of 16. See here: https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/1582

Supposedly, the new limit should be 12 (explained by limitations with the trait impls in the Rust standard library).

However, now I am actually investigating it, and it seems like the actual limit for system parameters in current bevy main is 11, not 12. The actual limit for query parameters is 14.

These numbers seem weird? Is this a bug/oversight? If yes, it should probably be fixed before releasing 0.5.
comments: @cart sanity check on whether this should block 0.5? Also to make sure migration guide advice is correct.
@cart Will this be addressed before 0.5? It seems like a weird minor oversight?
Yeah if SystemParams aren't lined up with the Default impls for rust tuples, they should be. WorldQuery impls shouldn't have the same limitations, so we can pick whatever makes sense there.

review_comments:
If clippy lets you, I'd consider making this
```rust
fn default_config() ->() {}
```
This is also fine however, the only confusion arises due to exactly reviewing this PR in the diff viewer 😅

```suggestion
all_tuples!(impl_system_function, 0..=16, F);
```
This was what I intended for the change to be, which makes the inclusiveness of the bounds explicit.
Yeah I like that. I'm probably going to merge this as-is, but feel free to follow up with that if you want.

👍 I accidentally suggested this, intending to suggest https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/1805#discussion_r606448919.

I did also want to suggest exactly this, but didn't know what the syntax would be so didn't attempt to, but actually did it by mistake.

I can't remember if this is efficiently implemented - it might be one of the range footguns.
It should be a small footgun, as it's not called with a long range and it's at compile time
I would rather not change the api this close to the release, with the blog, the migration guide and the cheat book mostly written / updated

That makes sense. I think that this current API is extremely ugly and I don't like the footgun of it only being limited to 16, and field ordering being significant

I'd personally rather see it changed before 0.5, but this PR isn't the place to decide that.

Yeah im open to considering alternatives, but probably not for 0.5. I generally just try to avoid creating new symbols via macros unless absolutely necessary. But it does feel necessary here / i wasn't properly considering the implications of this choice for the user-facing config api.
I'd be tempted to use some macros and make structs `T0,T1,...,T16`. However, this approach is also reasonable.

We also want to check big tuples used as system parameters, such as 
```rust
fn sys_y(_: (Local<T0>, Local<T1>, ..., Local<T16>), Query<&T> )
```
